Basement Remodeling to Turn Your Lower Level Into Real Living Space

RT Signature Homes Design & Build transforms unfinished and dated basements in Redmond and across the Eastside into comfortable, code-ready living space, coordinating layout, moisture control, egress, and finishes so your lower level works as hard as the rest of the home.

Request a consultation Explore design ideas
Call (206) 775-8077
Completed RT project pictured · Renton

Project fit

Basement finishing and remodeling, planned for comfort and code.

Whether your basement is unfinished, partially finished, or simply dated, we plan the space as a complete system — framing, insulation, moisture control, lighting, and finishes — so it feels like a natural part of the home rather than an afterthought below the stairs.

Typical scope

  • Full basement finishing and refinishing
  • Family rooms, rec rooms, and media spaces
  • Guest bedrooms, home offices, and flex rooms
  • Bathrooms, wet bars, and added storage
  • Egress, moisture control, insulation, and code coordination

Why choose us

Why Choose Us for Your Basement Remodeling Project

Dry and healthy first

A finished basement is only as good as the water and air management behind the walls, so we address moisture, drainage, and ventilation before any finish goes in.

Designed for real use

We plan layout, lighting, and ceiling height around how you will actually use the space, so a below-grade room still feels bright, comfortable, and inviting.

Code and egress handled

Bedrooms and living spaces below grade carry specific egress and code requirements, which we confirm with the local jurisdiction before design.

Design ideas

Turn an Unfinished Basement Into the Room Your Home Is Missing

A basement is often the most cost-effective way to add real living space without changing your home's footprint. The right plan turns dead storage into a family room, guest suite, home office, or whatever your household needs most.

Basement Living Ideas

Explore layouts for family rooms, guest suites, home offices, media rooms, and wet bars, planned with the lighting, storage, and flooring that make a lower level comfortable.

Explore the gallery

Design considerations

Design a Basement That Feels Bright, Warm, and Genuinely Usable

Below grade, thoughtful design does the heavy lifting. We plan layout and circulation around support posts, ductwork, and the stairs, and use layered lighting to make up for limited natural light.

Flooring, insulation, and materials are chosen for comfort and durability in a lower-level environment, with built-in storage and finishes that tie the space to the rest of your home.

The goal is a basement that reads as a real room, warm, finished, and functional, rather than a cold, utilitarian afterthought.

Below-grade essentials

Get the Basics Right Below Grade: Moisture, Ventilation, Egress, and Code

A lasting finished basement starts with the parts you do not see. We assess moisture and drainage, address any water intrusion, and plan vapor control and insulation suited to below-grade walls and slabs.

Ventilation, ceiling height, and headroom are evaluated early, and any bedroom or sleeping space is planned around egress-window and exit requirements for safety and code.

Permits and applicable building codes are confirmed with the local jurisdiction before construction, so the finished space is safe, legal, and built to last.

How the work moves

A process that keeps decisions ahead of construction.

Discovery and site assessment

We clarify goals, review existing conditions, identify constraints, and determine what needs deeper investigation before a scope is written.

Design and pre-construction

Layout, materials, trade requirements, permits, allowances, schedule factors, and decision deadlines are coordinated into one buildable plan.

Construction and completion

The work is sequenced, protected, inspected, communicated, and closed out with a final walkthrough and documented completion items.

Budget and schedule orientation

Scope the variables before suggesting a number.

Useful early guidance identifies what changes the investment and timeline. A responsible project range follows an assessment of the property, scope, finish expectations, and delivery constraints.

Common factors

  • Existing structural and mechanical conditions
  • Project size, layout changes, and finish level
  • Permit, engineering, and design requirements
  • Material availability and product lead times
  • Site access, protection, and project sequencing

Questions homeowners ask

Basement Remodeling FAQs

Is my basement a good candidate for finishing?

Most basements can be finished, but the right approach depends on ceiling height, moisture conditions, access, and existing systems. We assess these before design so the plan fits your specific lower level.

How do you handle basement moisture and water problems?

We identify the source of any moisture or water intrusion and address drainage and waterproofing before finishing. Vapor control, insulation, and ventilation suited to below-grade spaces are then planned into the design.

Can I add a bedroom or guest suite in the basement?

Often yes, but a below-grade sleeping room must meet egress requirements, typically an egress window or walkout and proper exits. We confirm the requirements with the local jurisdiction before committing to a layout.

Do basement remodels require permits?

Finishing or remodeling a basement generally requires permits and inspections, especially when adding bedrooms, bathrooms, electrical, or plumbing. We confirm the review path for your scope before construction.

What can I use a finished basement for?

Common uses include family and media rooms, guest bedrooms, home offices, gyms, playrooms, wet bars, and added storage. We plan the space around how your household wants to use it.

Tell us about your basement, how you want to use it, the ceiling height, and any moisture you have noticed.
